variants.note: A-B-B-B-A: advanced end and centre pavilions, recessed intermediate wall -- the style's own proportional_system bay_rhythm, stated directly.

bay_rhythm.value: A-B-B-B-A pavilion rhythm: advanced end bays and an advanced centre, regular intermediate rhythm between

composition_parti.note: The family's composition_parti slot deliberately leaves symmetry class open across all 21 members; this style is the one that most needs a real answer, and states it here without touching the family's additive-vernacular prohibition or its own rule sentence.
composition_parti.rule_append: End and centre pavilions advanced not less than 18 in from the intermediate wall plane -- c03, a hard constraint. A flat facade with applied ornament is Neoclassical Revival, not Beaux-Arts.

variants.note: distinguished_from[2]: 'Beaux-Arts is horizontal, Roman and French neoclassical in ornament, and terminates in a balustrade or attic rather than a roof.' defining_characteristics[2]: 'Deep entablature and heavily projecting cornice, usually surmounted by a balustrade or an attic storey'. c04: 'The composition must terminate above the cornice - balustrade, attic storey, or sculptural group - to a height of not less than 1/8 of the wall height.' It replaces beaux-arts-french's forbidden row ('own distinguished_from note against french-neoclassical is explicit: 'the invisible roof behind a balustrade is Neoclassical' -- Beaux-Arts reinstates 'a visible mansard or attic.''). Judgment on the id: the record names no roof form, and this is the corpus's id for a roof the balustrade hides.

Demoted from canonical, where beaux-arts-french put it ('own massing_affinities marks mansard-block canonical: 'the mansard returns as a fully occupiable attic and as the device that gives an otherwise flat-topped block a silhouette.' Also the crowning member of the base:shaft:attic three-part division named in defining_characteristics.'). This record's composition 'terminates in a balustrade or attic rather than a roof' and gives the steep roof to Chateauesque (distinguished_from[2]: 'Chateauesque is vertical, French Renaissance and late Gothic in ornament, and dominated by an enormous steep roof.'). But its own facade-pavilion binding reads 'Bound for the mansard and the pavilion' and 'The American Beaux-Arts house takes the French roof and the projecting end pavilion' (proportion_packs[4].note), and that pack dimensions this node's mansard: its `mansard_lower_slope` governs this kit's roof_pitch. The record's words are split, so the row is permitted and not forbidden; permitted rather than canonical is a judgment.

roof_form.rule: The composition terminates above the cornice in a balustrade, an attic storey or a sculptural group (c04), 'rather than a roof' (distinguished_from[2]); its facade-pavilion binding takes the French roof (proportion_packs[4].note).
roof_form.note: BOUND 1 Oct 2026 (WP-16.9), on Lucas's answer B1 of 30 Sep 2026, recorded in oq/the-roof-is-drawn-side-gabled-whatever-the-style-says: beaux-arts-american binds its own roof_form. Until then it wrote none and resolved BEAUX-ARTS-FRENCH's record: `mansard-block` canonical, noted 'own massing_affinities marks mansard-block canonical: 'the mansard returns as a fully occupiable attic and as the device that gives an otherwise flat-topped block a silhouette.' Also the crowning member of the base:shaft:attic three-part division named in defining_characteristics.', and `low-roof-behind-balustrade` FORBIDDEN, noted 'own distinguished_from note against french-neoclassical is explicit: 'the invisible roof behind a balustrade is Neoclassical' -- Beaux-Arts reinstates 'a visible mansard or attic.'' Both are the French node's reading of its own record. This record's words invert them in part: distinguished_from[2] 'Beaux-Arts is horizontal, Roman and French neoclassical in ornament, and terminates in a balustrade or attic rather than a roof.' In part, because its own facade-pavilion binding says 'The American Beaux-Arts house takes the French roof and the projecting end pavilion' (proportion_packs[4].note), and that pack's `mansard_lower_slope` governs this kit's roof_pitch; so the mansard is demoted to permitted, not forbidden. Neither form is one the roof layer draws, so the ruling's closed table says it rather than draws it, before and after; what moves is what the sheet says. Marked judgment for the id chosen for the hidden roof and for the mansard's rank. The mansard's rank, permitted rather than canonical or forbidden, is the independent check's amendment where the record's words are split: T9, taken as recommended under Lucas's standing instruction of 1 Oct 2026 ('Proceed with all recommended answers for all future questions in this session'); the question was never put to him, so this is not an answer he chose; recorded in oq/the-roof-is-drawn-side-gabled-whatever-the-style-says.

variants.note: American Beaux-Arts practice specifically: masonry-and-terracotta envelope wrapped around a modern iron/steel/reinforced-concrete frame, still detailed to genuine masonry-mass discipline -- the family note's own stated exception.

construction_type.note: The family (via continental-baroque-neoclassical) already states this correctly in prose; this delta only promotes the American steel-frame-plus-masonry-skin reading from a footnote to a named canonical variant, since it is how nearly every large Beaux-Arts American commission was actually built.

rustication.value: rusticated base not less than one full storey, joints 3/4 to 1-1/2 in deep

foundation_expression.rule: A rusticated ground storey with vermiculated or banded joints, under a smooth ashlar upper wall -- diagnostic_tells, matching the hard-constraint minimum storey height and joint depth in c02.

jamb_material.value: returned in the same material as the face

arch_construction.value: true voussoirs and keystones at arched openings

reveal_masonry.rule: Minimum 12 in reveal at openings, jambs returned in the same material as the face, arches with true voussoirs and keystones -- c02, a hard constraint.

garage_strategy.note: Not authored. Style status is 'historical' with no revival_periods and the style's own text states 'almost nobody can afford to build another' -- this is not a contemporary buildable node in the sense docs/inheritance.md's garage_strategy guidance targets (20th-century-forward, actively built work).

variants.note: Primary bound pack (vignola-composite). The imperial, triumphal-arch register the style's own lineage names directly.
The domestic register for the Newport houses (Marble House, Rosecliff), both quoting Corinthian-ordered French royal models.
c01: 'Orders must be executed to a published canon...An order without a full entablature is void.'

order.rule: Executed to a published canon (Vignola) with entasis, correct capital, base and entablature -- c01. Frequently paired or coupled rather than single, which is the style's fastest diagnostic tell against Neoclassical Revival.
order.note: Overrides an incorrect cascade: the lineage walk lands on french-vernacular (via a distant reference edge) and forbids the entire classical-apparatus group with a rule true of vernacular farm buildings and false of this style, whose hard constraint c01 makes the order the single most load-bearing fact in the kit.

variants.note: diagnostic_tells: 'Paired or coupled columns and pilasters. Neoclassical Revival uses single columns; pairing is the fastest Beaux-Arts marker.'
Where the composition genuinely calls for a single order, but this is the Neoclassical Revival reading and should be rare here.

coupled_clear_spacing.note: Diameters clear between a coupled pair, per the style's own proportional_system typical_ratios.

column.rule: Paired or coupled far more often than single -- the style's fastest diagnostic tell.

cornice_projection_min.value: not less than the entablature depth

entablature.rule: Entablature depth 1/5 to 1/4 of column height; cornice projection not less than the entablature depth -- c01, a hard constraint. Deep and heavily projecting, per defining_characteristics.

pediment.rule: Subordinate to the pavilion-and-attic composition the style actually terminates in (c04); a pediment is one available device among several, not the primary skyline move.

variants.note: Articulates the recessed wall plane between advanced pavilions -- c03.

pilaster.rule: Runs the recessed intermediate wall between the advanced end and centre pavilions that c03 requires.

presence.value: present wherever the entablature is bound; scaled to the monumental cornice, not the domestic one
presence.note: EDITORIAL, AND NO SOURCE IS RECORDED (OQ 18, annotated 25 Aug 2026; reclassified 25 Aug after audit). The basis stated for this slot is: "A full modillion or dentil course runs with the deep, heavily projecting cornice defining_characteristics describes -- this is the entablature's own module at the roofline, not a separate invention." -- which is the reasoning, not a citation. A CATEGORICAL CALL, NOT A MEASUREMENT -- it names a treatment or a class, so no citation would sharpen it into a number. What it needs is a source showing the tradition makes this choice, not a figure.

modillion_dentil.rule: A full modillion or dentil course runs with the deep, heavily projecting cornice defining_characteristics describes -- this is the entablature's own module at the roofline, not a separate invention.

variants.note: c04: the composition must terminate above the cornice -- balustrade, attic storey, or sculptural group -- to a height not less than 1/8 of the wall height.
c04: 'A cornice that simply stops leaves the style unfinished.' This is precisely the move distinguished_from names against chateauesque, which terminates in a roof instead.

balustrade.rule: The skyline is populated -- balustrades, urns, statuary, attic cartouches -- per diagnostic_tells, and is a hard-adjacent constraint (c04, soft severity) that the cornice never simply stops at.

variants.note: defining_characteristics: 'swags, cartouches, garlands, keystone masks, and free-standing figures on the skyline.'
Adam/Federal register, a different and later academic tradition.

ornament_vocabulary.rule: Abundant sculptural ornament in quantity, executed by hand at a density that would be oppressive at domestic scale -- swags, cartouches, garlands, keystone masks, skyline figures.
